newsitem.title: USA: GE pays U.S. in misrepresentation case.
newsitem.headline: GE pays U.S. in misrepresentation case.

text.p: General Electric Co has paid $950,000 to the U.S. government for alleged false representations concerning aircraft engines supplied to the government, the Justice Department said Friday.

The department said General Electric sold hundreds of aircraft engines with control circuit boards that had not undergone the required tests. In delivering the engines, GE said it completed the tests, the department said in a statement.

"Defense contractors should be forewarned that the Department of Defense and the Department of Justice are determined to investigate and prosecute any misdeeds by those who win government contracts," Assistant Attorney General Frank Hunger said.
The procedures that GE failed to perform were ionic cleanliness, electrostatic discharge and solder purity tests, the statement said.
General Electric notified the Department of Defense of the false representations under a voluntary disclosure program.
